chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Bakr ibn Salih, from Ibn Fazzal, from Abdullah ibn Ibrahim, from Ali ibn Abu Ali al-Lahabi, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:
He (peace be upon him) said: 'What do your physicians say regarding the evening meal?' I said, 'They forbid us from it.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'But I command you to have it.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on eating dinner at night according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) contrasts the medical opinion of forbidding late-night meals with his own religious recommendation to eat dinner, emphasizing the spiritual and physical merit of the evening meal over strict medical caution. This hadith highlights the Shia scholarly principle that religious prescriptions often prioritize holistic well-being and prophetic tradition over rigid medical dogma, encouraging believers to maintain regular nourishment for sustenance in worship.
